Letter of Permanent Representation

Delivered to the President of the General Assembly, 24 February 2026. Subject: Statement on the reform of the United Nations Secretariat.

Your Excellency,

I have the honour to write to you on behalf of my Government, which has occupied a seat at this Assembly for forty-one consecutive years, to convey concern regarding several matters touching the organization, and to offer observations that my Government trusts will be given their due weight.

I. On the scale of the Secretariat

The establishment of the Secretariat as presently constituted is a matter on which my Government has taken a clear and, I will be candid, unpopular position at every Fifth Committee session in which it has arisen. The organization now maintains a staff establishment of approximately 44,000, of which some 31,000 are deployed in field locations. My Government notes with concern that the growth in field establishment has not been matched by proportionate growth in the substantive output delivered to this Assembly.

I should say clearly that my Government does not dispute the value of the organization's humanitarian work. It has seen the work. My Government's concern is one of proportion, and my Government would ask that proportion be defended by those who set it.

II. On mandate design

A mandate that cannot be enforced is not a mandate; it is a description. My Government has observed that a number of mandates adopted in recent sessions would not survive contact with a serious audit, and that the principal obstacle to such an audit is not the absence of authority but the presence of inertia.

The pattern is well known to every delegation in this Hall. A mandate is adopted, it is not implemented, it is renewed, it is not implemented, and the renewal is recorded in a report whose authors would not characterise the outcome as a success if pressed to do so.

III. On the views of non-member States

My Government wishes to place on record its regret at the tendency of certain delegations to treat the views of States not represented in the Security Council as, at best, of academic interest. This is not a legal objection. It is an observation about what this organization has become.

IV. On the humanitarian component

My Government reaffirms its support for the humanitarian operations under the organization's auspices and would urge that no reduction in the humanitarian mandate be contemplated as part of any budgetary adjustment.

The remainder of this letter concerns the composition and functioning of the Secretariat and shall not be read as directed at the humanitarian component.

V. Conclusion

My Government would be glad to be helpful in the search for a structure that is proportionate to the purposes the Charter sets out, and remains ready to consult in good faith in due course.

I beg to renew, Your Excellency, the assurances of my Government’s highest consideration.

[Signature block: Permanent Representative of [State] to the United Nations]
